sections.h2: What does the Mecklenburg County Register of Deeds do?
sections.html:
The office records, indexes and stores the real estate and business documents presented for registration in Mecklenburg County. A sale in Charlotte or any of the county's towns is not complete against outsiders until the deed is recorded there.

The county describes the real estate side of the office as the official repository for public records on property in Mecklenburg County. Documents include conveyances, deeds of trust and mortgages, powers of attorney, assumed names, separation agreements and maps or plats. The same office issues marriage licenses, administers notary oaths, records DD-214 military discharges and keeps birth, death and marriage records.

Visitors can search the public records in the vault area from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. during office hours. For the street address of the recording counter and holiday closings, check the office website before you travel.

sections.h2: Why does recording a deed matter in North Carolina?
sections.html:
Because the date and time of registration decide priority. Under G.S. 47-18, a conveyance, option, lease of more than three years or right of first refusal does not bind lien creditors or purchasers for value until it is registered in the county where the land lies. Priority follows the order of registration.

For a Mecklenburg seller the practical result is simple. Until the buyer's deed is on record, a creditor of the seller or a second buyer could still claim a better position. Ask your closing attorney when the deed will be sent for recording.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a deed in Mecklenburg County?
sections.html:
A general instrument such as a deed costs $26 for the first 15 pages, and a deed of trust or mortgage costs $64 for the first 35 pages. Each added page costs $4 in both cases. These are the county's posted Uniform Fee Schedule amounts, which follow G.S. 161-10.

Mecklenburg County recording and copy fees, Uniform Fee Schedule
ItemFee as posted
Deed or other instrument$26 first 15 pages, $4 each page after
Deed of trust or mortgage$64 first 35 pages, $4 each page after
Plat$21 per sheet
Non-standard document$25 added to other fees
Extra instrument in one filing$10 each
Satisfaction of a deed of trustNo fee
Certified copy$5 first page, $2 each page after

Excessive index data adds $2 for each party name above 20. Plain copies are 25 cents a page in person and $1 a page by mail.

sections.h2: How must a document be formatted to be recorded?
sections.html:
It must meet the page standards in G.S. 161-14(b), or the office records it after charging the $25 non-standard fee. The county lists the rules in plain terms.

  • Paper size of 8.5 by 11 or 8.5 by 14 inches.
  • A blank 3-inch margin at the top of the first page, and quarter-inch margins on the other sides of that page and on every side of later pages.
  • Black type or print on white paper, no smaller than 9 points. Blanks and corrections may be made in pen.
  • One-sided pages, with the type of instrument stated at the top of page one.

If you prepare a document yourself, check it against this list before you submit it.

sections.h2: What are the steps from a signed deed to a recorded one in Mecklenburg County?
sections.html:
Four things have to line up before the clerk accepts a deed: the document meets the format rules, the excise tax is paid, the recording fee is paid, and the deed is presented to the county where the land lies. State law makes the fee schedule "complete and exclusive" and says fees are collected before filing, so there is no negotiating at the counter.

  • Confirm the deed names the correct grantor, and match the legal description to the prior deed in the vault records.
  • Have the seller's side pay the excise tax at the rate in G.S. 105-228.30.
  • Add the recording fee for the page count, plus any non-standard or extra-instrument fee.
  • Present the original, and keep the recording stamp or confirmation for your file.

When a payoff is involved, the lender's satisfaction is recorded at no fee, so a clean title picture shows up in the index after the closing.

sections.h2: What other records does the Mecklenburg County Register of Deeds handle for homeowners?
sections.html:
The office also records DD-214 military discharges, issues marriage licenses and keeps vital records. The Census Bureau counts 44,881 veterans in Mecklenburg County for 2020 to 2024, so the discharge recording service reaches many households.

The disabled veteran property tax exclusion is a separate filing. Applicants complete Form NCDVA-9 with a Veterans Service Officer and file with the county assessor, not with the Register of Deeds. State law removes the first $45,000 of appraised value for a qualifying veteran, and the program has no age or income limit. For deed questions, call the register's office. For value and exemption questions, contact the county Office of Tax Administration.

The register of deeds is an elected county office under G.S. 161-1, chosen every two years by county voters. A title question about a specific house belongs with a closing attorney.

sections.h2: How much is the transfer tax on a Mecklenburg County sale?
sections.html:
The state excise tax is $1.00 for each $500 of consideration or value, or fraction of $500, and the seller pays it. G.S. 105-228.30 says the transferor pays the register of deeds in the county where the property sits before the instrument is recorded.

The register collects it at recording. One half goes to the county general fund, and the other half goes to the Department of Revenue after refunds and the county's allowance. Ask your closing attorney for the figure on your price, because the tax depends on the consideration stated for your deed.

Mecklenburg County has a population of 1,233,383 as of July 1, 2025, and the Census Bureau lists a 2020 to 2024 median owner-occupied home value of $406,800. The same table shows 55.1 percent of homes owner-occupied and a median gross rent of $1,627, so renters hold a large share of the county's housing.

sections.h2: How do I pay and how can I protect my title records?
sections.html:
In person, the office accepts cash, Mastercard, Visa and Discover, checks and money orders, and escrow accounts for authorized users. Checks must carry the drawer's printed name and address and be payable to the Mecklenburg County Register of Deeds. Starter and counter checks are refused, and a returned check can bring a $35 processing fee.

The office also offers a free Property Fraud Alert that notifies you whenever a document bearing your name is recorded. That helps owners who hold a vacant or inherited house, where a forged deed would otherwise go unseen. A buyer under a contract for deed should note that Chapter 47H requires the seller to record the contract or a memorandum of it within five business days.

If you own a Mecklenburg house with unpaid taxes, a title problem or a difficult tenant, a cash buyer can close on the timeline that suits you and handle the recording through a closing attorney.

faqs.q: How much does a Mecklenburg County deed recording cost?
faqs.a: A general deed costs $26 for the first 15 pages plus $4 for each added page. A deed of trust or mortgage costs $64 for the first 35 pages plus $4 per added page. A non-standard document adds $25.

faqs.q: Who pays the North Carolina excise tax on a house sale?
faqs.a: The seller pays it. State law puts the duty on the transferor, who pays the register of deeds in the county where the land lies before the deed is recorded. The rate is $1.00 per $500 of value or fraction of it.

faqs.q: Is there a fee to record a satisfaction of my mortgage?
faqs.a: No. The Uniform Fee Schedule lists satisfaction instruments at no fee. Ask your lender to file the satisfaction after payoff and check later that it was recorded.

faqs.q: Can I search Mecklenburg County property records myself?
faqs.a: Yes. The public may search the records in the vault area from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. during office hours, and the county also posts a real estate records search on the Register of Deeds website.

faqs.q: What happens if my deed is not typed to the county's standards?
faqs.a: The office still records it, but it adds a $25 non-standard fee on top of the normal fees. Margins, 9-point minimum type and one-sided pages are the usual causes.
